text: Your inbox is chaos. Ads, newsletters, personal messages – a messy mix. You just want order, to find what matters without endless scrolling.
Suddenly, your inbox split. 'Promotions,' 'Social,' 'Updates' – neat tabs, sorting everything. But why? Who decided this was the best way to organize your mail?
You might assume it's just smart AI, anticipating your needs for ease. But this isn't about tidiness. It’s a deeper, more invisible goal, shaping your digital life.
The system learns from millions of users, categorizing emails by sender patterns. Its core aim? Separate urgent human messages from predictable, often commercial, noise.
This convenience has a cost: you now expect less from 'other' folders. Your attention is segmented, making you less likely to engage with anything not 'primary'.
Tomorrow, your inbox still sorts. But now you see the hidden hand, not just tidying, but subtly directing your digital focus and daily interactions.
